resources.string: Use the computer's IP address instead of its name, or start the harness with --trusted-host.
Enter the computer's IP address and a port between 1 and 65535.
Nothing answered at %1$s. The computer's firewall is probably blocking incoming connections on port %2$d. Allow it and try again. Some routers also stop Wi-Fi devices from reaching wired ones.
%1$s refused the connection. The harness only listens on the computer itself unless LAN mode is on. Turn it on and restart the harness. If you changed the port, check that it matches.
Nothing on this network answers to “%1$s”. Use the computer's IP address instead. To find it, run ipconfig on Windows, ip addr on Linux, or ifconfig on macOS.
Something answered at %1$s, but it isn't a DeepSeek Harness. Check the port the harness printed at startup.

%1$s answered, but the secure (HTTPS) connection failed. If your proxy uses a local certificate authority, install its CA certificate on this phone. If the address doesn't serve HTTPS, connect without https://.
%1$s is a harness, but it hasn't signed this phone in. Open the harness startup link on this device once, then connect again.
